name: Non-familial Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Heart Association Diagnostic Criteria for Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Left ventricular wall thickness ≥15 mm in adults without other causes of hypertrophy
No family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or related genetic mutations
Exclusion of secondary causes of hypertrophy such as hypertension or valvular disease
Asymmetric septal hypertrophy or other characteristic echocardiographic features
ECG abnormalities consistent with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (e.g., Q waves, repolarization changes)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy ≥15 mm without family history or secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be negative in non-familial cases; diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and exclusion of other causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic thickening of interventricular septum detected by imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
pathognomonic.notes: Obstruction caused by systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve

common.notes: Shortness of breath on physical activity due to impaired diastolic function
Chest pain due to myocardial ischemia despite normal coronary arteries
Awareness of abnormal heartbeats, often due to arrhythmias
Transient loss or near loss of consciousness related to arrhythmias or outflow obstruction

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to reduced cardiac output
occasional.notes: Generalized tiredness due to impaired cardiac function
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

occasional.notes: Signs of congestive heart failure in advanced disease
Breathlessness at night due to pulmonary congestion

rare.notes: Fatal arrhythmias leading to unexpected death
Embolic events related to atrial fibrillation
searchTerms: brain blood flow blockage due to clot

rare.notes: Leakage of mitral valve due to systolic anterior motion

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; BNP may be elevated in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing asymmetric septal hypertrophy and left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
Cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis
genetic: Absence of pathogenic sarcomeric gene mutations typical of familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities including Q waves, left ventricular hypertrophy patterns, and arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Regression of hypertrophy with blood pressure control
Physiological hypertrophy with normal diastolic function
No left ventricular outflow tract obstruction

redFlags: Family history of sudden cardiac death despite negative genetic testing
Progressive heart failure symptoms despite therapy
references: Maron BJ, et al. Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Present and Future, J Am Coll Cardiol. 2020
Elliott PM, et al. 2014 ESC Guidelines on diagnosis and management of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, Eur Heart J. 2014
